profile.name: Bill Truong
profile.title: Unity Engineer · Games, XR & Tools
profile.about: Unity engineer who makes games: mobile, VR multiplayer, game jams and browser builds. I write gameplay systems, multiplayer and shaders, tune performance for Meta Quest and low-end phones, and build the tools that keep a team moving. Outside Unity I build web apps, automation pipelines and AI agents.

companies.name: GEM CORPORATION
companies.story: Working with a client team on the design and build of a real-time data sync system for their platform.

companies.name: GAMELOFT
companies.story: Gameloft is where I learned how a large studio ships. I worked on the Treasure Toss and Animalody modules of Applaydu (50M+ downloads on Google Play), learned to read an unfamiliar codebase, and got used to code review and QA cycles against the licensor's standards. The photo is my desk from that time.

companies.name: FPT IS (akaVerse)
companies.story: At akaVerse I moved between games, VR, digital twins and 3D tooling. For a heritage project that digitized more than 30,000 artifacts, I wrote a cleanup tool that let artists process 10 to 20 scans per batch instead of one at a time, which helped a team of 10+ artists get through the archive in about three months. I also worked on real-time data sync and VR controls for an NVIDIA Omniverse digital twin that FPT Japan showed at NVIDIA AI Summit Tokyo 2024, where Jensen Huang tried the demo. I left when the work shifted toward industrial 3D outsourcing, because I wanted to stay close to games.

companies.name: CURLY BLUE
companies.role: Unity XR Developer, then Technical Artist
companies.story: When I joined, Shmackle used flat unlit assets. I rebuilt the look with toon, outline and dissolve shaders, then cut draw calls, instanced and atlased until the game held its 72 FPS baseline on Quest 2 and ran at roughly 80 to 90 FPS on Quest 3. I also built the Shmackle Pad, the in-game tablet for customization, social features and the store. On Teabag I owned the cel-shading pipeline, XR dynamic resolution and the modular wardrobe system. That work got me promoted to Technical Artist.

companies.name: GOLDEN SEA STUDIO
companies.story: A small studio making hyper-casual games on roughly one-month cycles. Tasks came in, we agreed on scope, and I built them, including Merge Fruit from prototype to release. I learned to work fast, cut scope early and keep builds small.

companies.name: MARATHON EDU
companies.story: Part-time. I helped students learning computer science pick a learning path and work through the problems they were stuck on.

productions.name: KINDLY'S PROMISE
productions.desc: Narrative sci-fi adventure, vertical slice (Unity URP)
productions.story: A vertical slice I built alone to test stylized rendering on URP. It has a modular interaction system, a branching dialogue engine, a see-through dissolve that uses the stencil buffer to reveal the player behind walls, cel shading and interactive foliage.

productions.name: SHMACKLE VR
productions.role: Unity XR Developer, then Technical Artist
productions.desc: Multiplayer VR social sandbox on Meta Quest
productions.story: I rebuilt the game's look with toon, outline and dissolve shaders while holding 72 FPS on Quest 2. I built the Shmackle Pad (the in-game tablet for customization, social and store), worked on the Shooting Range update with Photon Fusion, and added a dynamic FOV option to reduce motion sickness.

productions.name: ANIMAL PUSH ROYALE
productions.story: I worked on gameplay, onboarding, UI, shaders and performance. When the project lost its level lead, I took over more of the game and made the technical and gameplay calls. It reached the Top 6 at Vietnam GameVerse 2024.

productions.name: BILL BIOME SHADER
productions.story: This suite uses GPU instancing for dense environments, with interactive foliage and an in-editor painting tool.

productions.name: BILL SSOUTLINE
productions.story: A screen-space outline render feature built on URP's Render Graph. A plain Sobel pass draws lines where objects overlap; I added depth and normal sensitivity checks to remove those artifacts.

productions.name: AKAVERSE TWIN
productions.story: I worked on real-time data sync and VR controls for an Omniverse digital twin demo. FPT Japan presented it at NVIDIA AI Summit Tokyo 2024, and Jensen Huang tried it on the show floor.

productions.name: APPLAYDU
productions.story: I wrote gameplay for the Treasure Toss and Animalody modules and iterated on them with designers and QA until they met the licensor's bar.
